Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph FEB 1 0 2020 OPINION NO. Æ__ S. 20 QO RAMIL D. MAQUILAN Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Pantukan, Compostela Valley Chairman, Committee on Housing, Zoning, Urban & Rural Development Dear Mr. Maquilan: This has reference to the letter you sent dated 22 November 2019, requesting for this Department's legal opinion regarding disposition through donation to Davao del Norte Electric Cooperative ("DANECO") of a 2, 100 square meters of land intended for the Cultural Communities Village or Mansaka Village. In your letter, a brief background of the facts states that in 2008, the local government unit ("LGU") of Pantukan bought a parcel of land with an area of more or less 9.4634 hectares located at Townsite, Kingking, Pantukan, Compostela Valley. Of the total area, 16,982 square meters were allotted for Cultural Communities Village as shown in Resolution No. 06, series of 2009. Furthermore, it also stated in Resolution No. 49, series of 2008, that the Municipal Government of Pantukan has purchased a 9.4 hectares land intended as resettlement area as well as a portion for the Mansaka Village and the rest for the Employees Village. Additionally, Resolution No. 269, series of 2018 states that the Indegenous People of Pantukan were given the right to develop the said area for the advancement of their socio-economic and cultural aspects. However, in a letter dated 16 September 2019 from the Davao del Norte Electric Cooperative ("DANECO"), a company performing proprietary functions, thru its General Manager, is asking the LGU to donate 2,000 square meters of land for the construction of IOMVA Substation and 100 square meters lot for the Switchyard which shall be taken from the land allotted for the Cultural Communities or Mansaka Village. The SB Members are willing to give authority to the Mayor to donate said lands. Under this premise arose the request for clarification on whether or not it is valid to donate the area intended for the Cultural Communities Village to DANECO. At the outset, we deem it proper to cite the pertinent provisions of Republic Act No. 7160, as amended otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 ("LGC") regarding the right of LGUs to acquire properties for welfare purposes and, development, to wit:

"SECTION 18. Power to Generate and Apply Resources. — Local government units shall have the power and authority to xxx to acquire, deve10L lease, encumber, alienate, or otherwise dispose of real or personal property held by them in their proprietary capacity and to apply their resources and assets for productive, developmental, or welfare purposes, in the exercise or furtherance of their qovernmental or proprietary powers and functions and thereby ensure their development into self- reliant communities and active participants in the attainment of national goals. " [Emphasis and underscoring supplied]. Accordingly, in 2008, the LGU of Pantukan bought a parcel of land with a total area of 9.4634 hectares, located at Townsite, Kingking, Pantukan, Compostela Valley for the purpose of establishing a resettlement area for socialized housing as well as allotting a portion thereof for the Cultural Communities Village as per Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No.06, series of 2009 and SB Resolution No. 49, series of 2008. Correspondingly, in Resolution No. 269, series of 2018, the LGU of Pantukan confirms the Certificate of Award given to the Indigenous People of Pantukan as proof that they are the recipient of "Lot-C" or the parcel of land consisting a total area of 16,982 square meters. Similarly, it is imperative to mention that under the LGC, LGUs are prohibited to devote public property for private purposes and the funds shall only be applied for the particular purpose for its allotment, to wit: "SECTION 335. Prohibitions Against Expenditures for Religious or Private Purposes. — No public money or P.C..Q2ßCtY shall be appropriated or applied for religious SECTION 336. Use of Appropriated Funds and Savings. — Funds shall be available exclusively for the specific ur ose for which the have been ro riate xxx xxx xxx [Emphasis and underscoring supplied]. In view of the foregoing, this Department is of the considered view that the LGU cannot donate any part of the parcel of land it acquired which was already given to the Indigenous People as it will not be in accordance with the purpose on why such property was acquired by the LGU in the first place, which was to develop the said area for the advancement of their socio-economic and cultural aspects. Furthermore, considering that the would-be donee is DANECO, a company performing proprietary

functions, such act of donation would be violative of the above-cited provision on the restriction or prohibition of appropriating property for private purpose. At the same time, considering that this Department does not have a copy of the Resolution granting the Certificate of Award, We are unable to fully determine its nature and on whether the Indigenous People of Pantukan already have vested rights over said portion of land. Also, it it is noteworthy to mention that the granting of the Certificate of Award was done only through a resolution and not an ordinance. A resolution is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a law-making body on a specific matter and is temporary in nature and the CLUP, through an ordinance, can change the use of the property. On the contrary, that there is already a vested right over the said portion of property, this Department is of the opinion that to reduce such portion would be violative of the non-impairment clause guaranteed under the 1987 Philipppine Constitution. Verily, while it is ingrained in jurisprudence that the constitutional prohibition does not prohibit every change in existing laws, to fall within the prohibition, the change must be substantial or must effect a change in the rights of the parties. Such as in the case of reducing the total awarded area to the Cultural Communities Village, there would be substantial impairment as the donation to DANECO would authorize something different from that provided in the terms of the Resolution considering that DANECO would use the property in constructing substations and switchyard which will involve large number of machineries and will occupy huge amount of space and in effect diminish the efficacy of the award of the property to the Indigenous People. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Ve rul ours, M. ANO Secretary COPY FURNISHED: ALEX C.
